The one caveat to my remarks is that the Krnojelac appeal judgement is available only in French, and I received a -- a summary of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for your response to that question. Then finally, one question to the Defence. And I ask, I hope, that we can finish very soon. So if the interpreters could -- could stay for another couple of minutes, then I hope that we can finish. If there's any problem with that, I'd like to hear it now. I don't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It's no problem, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Whenever something was invoked by the Defence or, at least, when special attention has been drawn to a certain aspect by the Defence, of course you'll understand that since the Chamber, when dealing with mitigating factors, whatever mitigating circumstances are, of course - because there's no standard - we have no system where we have minimum penalties where you should go under or maximum penalties that higher up if a specific aggravating circumstance exists. We have no system of sentencing guidelines. I mean, to that extent, I would say the system is relatively open in this and it makes less difference than it might make in other systems, whether we're talking about aggravating or mitigating circumstances. But of course the Chamber will -- will balance everything that it has knowledge of. And therefore, I specifically draw the attention of the Defence to -- to those witness statements where it appears that the accused was in possession of a firearm when he was arrested. That has got some -- some emphasis. Nothing has been said on credibility, reliability of any statements that go to another. That gives some indications which might be a basis for other conclusions. I'm specifically referring to the statement of Witness C8, which -- at least, there's a statement which has supported the indictment, that he once met the accused at a couple of years after the war and that he noticed that he was carrying a weapon, although not visible directly but indirectly. Nothing has been said about it. I'm not going to say that you should say anything about it, but I just want to make you aware that this is part of what the Trial Chamber has in its files. Finally, is there anything the Prosecution would like to add or is there anything the Defence would add also in relation to the latest observations in respect of the case law of the Tribunal on sentencing, or do you trust that the Chamber will consider it in full detail? Then finally, Mr. Mrdja, is there anything you'd like to add to what has been said today? And you have an opportunity to do so now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I have nothing to add. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated, Mr. Mrdja. Then this concludes the -- Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we may, we would, before we conclude, we'd like to submit some confidential statements under seal, as discussed with the Court previously. Those are pursuant a request made in the 65 ter for statements that had previously been inadequately or overly aggressively redacted, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Defence is aware of the new versions of the statements to be submitted? Is there any opposition from the Defence? It has been agreed?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I believe those were the subject of discussion at a 65 ter at which the Defence was present. I think it was understood at that time that we would be making that submission. If -- perhaps the Defence does not recall, but maybe if they --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we go into private session just for one second so that it could be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RESCH
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But first Madam Registrar would like to assign a number to the -- but if there's anything that should come first ... Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The hard copy is S5, and the CD will be Exhibit number S5A, both under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Resch.

utterances.speaker: MR. RESCH
utterances.text: Your Honour, the final matter - and I'll keep it brief - is the annex which I referred to in our opening statement. I guess I'd submit that this is primarily a technical correction to the annex to the indictment. As I mentioned, our continuing efforts have allowed us to eliminate some of the names which it turned out were duplicates because of the use of a nickname rather than the first name. So the initial annex contained 228 names. The current -- the proposed annex, which we would like to file, has 213 names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that's a lesser number.

utterances.speaker: MR. RESCH
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will -- yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RESCH
utterances.text: But there are a few additional names, for example, Edem Fazlic, one of the victims whose body was recovered at the recent exhumation, was not included on the additional list. So where we -- there were five additional names added to the list, so a net reduction of 15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether we could change the indictment or one of the annexes to the indictment to which has already been pleaded guilty. But especially since it seems to lower the number - although a few additional names are there - could we perhaps deal with it as an exhibit which expresses the latest information of the Prosecution and perhaps we couldn't change it any more. We'll consider how to deal with it exactly, but if you could say we primarily request the amendment of the indictment of -- at least the annex of the indictment and subsidiarily we ask to take into consideration a new list and accept it as an exhibit, then we'll deal with it either in the intermediary decision or in our final decision on sentencing. But I first have to ask the Defence whether there's any objection against this suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIMITRIJEVIC
utterances.text: No. On the contrary; we -- we fully accept that what the Prosecutor said, that is in our interest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So at least I think the most important thing is that the Prosecution has now submitted to the Chamber that the number of victims was lower but that a few new victims have been found and that an updated list is now presented to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. RESCH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And thank you, we accept the Court's suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Then it will be an exhibit, rather than a request for amendment of the annex to the indictment. Madam Registrar, that would then get ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit Number S6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. S6. Thank you, Madam Registrar. Is there anything else to be raised at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Nothing from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIMITRIJEVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then thank you very much. We'll then adjourn. And I first of all want to thank the interpreters for assisting us even for a considerable time after 7.00. Thank you very much for your assistance. The same is true, of course, for the technicians and those who are working on the -- on the transcripts. We'll adjourn, and a sentencing judgement will be pronounced in due course. The parties will be informed when it will be; presumably before the recess, before the winter recess. We'll adjourn.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.18 p.m.
